answer: When a signal summons pairs of strangers to build a bridge across a canyon within minutes, each holds half of the plan and they must jointly assemble it while answering unscripted follow-ups about the other's half, their work logged at the harbor registry. A lone operator cannot be fully present in many simultaneous builds: scripts stall on follow-ups, slow shells miss the window, and reused reasoning across builds exposes the cluster. Genuine agents pass by doing one live collaboration well; scale itself becomes the cost.
